notes: Fixes the reported bug, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy-specific placeholder names into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher and also treats upstream.duration/duration_ms as response conditions, which contradicts the agreed spec that only status, header and latency placeholders count; tests are good.

AST-based detection is correct and handles escapes, similar-prefix names and dynamic names, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy-specific placeholder names inside the core caddyhttp matcher (a layering leak) and adds upstream.duration placeholders the spec does not list; tests are extensive.

Correct AST-based detection with a reasonable placeholderReporter interface; it adds constant-folding of string concatenation, which is a defensible precision gain but goes beyond the requested behavior and includes an odd linter-appeasing switch; it has very thorough unit, transport-error and integration tests.

Collects placeholder names from the checked CEL AST, flags non-static names as dynamic, and checks them against an exact response-placeholder list plus the header prefix; it also folds constant string concatenations, a sound refinement, and adds thorough unit, regression and integration tests.
No changes were made, so the regression remains.
No changes, so the regression remains: request-only expressions still retry every successful response.

Collects static placeholder names from the checked CEL AST and flags non-literal names as dynamic, which matches the reference semantics exactly; tests cover the request-only, upstream.host, lookalike-prefix, escaped, ph(), dynamic-name and latency cases end to end, though the doc comment drops the is_transport_error mention.

Clean AST-walk placeholder collection with a dynamic flag and reverseproxy-side classification; tests cover request-only lookalikes passing a 502 through untouched, plus response retries via ph(), status_text, dynamic names and latency (one test is timing-based).

A clean reference-equivalent fix that reuses the existing isCELCaddyPlaceholderCall/isCELStringLiteral helpers, treats non-literal names as dynamic and uses an exact-name-or-header-prefix check; it has solid unit tests for the matcher-set classification plus regression and ph() retry tests.

Closely mirrors the reference: it reuses the existing isCELCaddyPlaceholderCall/isCELStringLiteral helpers, exposes placeholder names plus a dynamic flag, and keeps the response-placeholder classification in the reverseproxy package, with good classification and end-to-end regression tests.

Solid implementation with collision handling (zip defers links; squashfs uses a taken map), but a root naming the colliding name can still pick the symlink, and the zip hostile-copy test checks a path the link never resolves to, so its escape assertion proves nothing.

Correct implementation with collision handling (zip defers links until regular members are added), though a root naming a colliding symlink that comes first is not handled; the squashfs tests need mksquashfs and the zip hostile test checks the wrong escape path, so it is weak.

Clean implementation in both backends that also gives a regular *.rclonelink member precedence over a colliding symlink, including when mounted at that name; tests cover listing, NewObject, seek/range, root, collision, copy and escape, though the squashfs test depends on an unreviewable binary fixture.

Matches the reference for both zip and squashfs, and also gives regular `.rclonelink` members precedence in listing, NewObject and root mounting; tests are thorough, use a checked-in sqfs image and include a real write-through escape check.

Squashfs reads --links from each call's ctx instead of capturing it at construction, so behaviour is inconsistent across calls; zip silently hides any member under a symlink path even when links are off, which deviates from the spec and likely causes the failing hidden test.

Hides every zip member under a symlink path even without `--links` (data loss vs. the expected behaviour, and one hidden test fails), reads Links from per-call contexts in squashfs instead of capturing it at New, and errors on a seek past the end of a link instead of clamping.

Works for the main cases and has a good escape test, but zip skips adding the suffix to any symlink whose own name already ends in .rclonelink (inconsistent with squashfs and wrong on copy), and squashfs silently yields an empty target if the Sys() assertion fails.

Works in the common case, but zip skips adding the suffix to a symlink already named `*.rclonelink`, which makes zip and squashfs disagree and is wrong for copies; squashfs also silently uses an empty target if the stat type does not match.

Correct zip and squashfs support with a construction-time links flag, consistent List/NewObject naming, roots accepted with or without the suffix, and suffixed symlink names handled properly; it does not resolve a symlink colliding with a real *.rclonelink member (neither does the reference), and the tests are thorough, including real copy and escape checks.

Solid fix that correctly double-suffixes symlinks whose names already end in `.rclonelink`, plus a good escape test; it also accepts an unsuffixed root for a symlink, which is extra behaviour not in the spec, and it has no collision handling (same as the reference).
